preamble: The elision of [m] is a widespread historical process, particularly at the ends of words or before fricatives. It typically involves a stage of vowel nasalization followed by the complete loss of the consonantal gesture. In Australia, initial *m was lost in Northern Paman languages such as Angkamuthi Uradhi (ayi < *mayi 'vegetable food') and Mpalitjanh (arta < *mara 'hand').

examples.note: Final m was lost very early in Vulgar Latin speech.
Nasal Spirant Law: loss of nasal before a fricative with compensatory lengthening.
Word-final Proto-Samic *m was lost in Northern Sami; Inari Sami eennâm and Skolt Sami jânnam keep it.
Compare Inari Sami kietkâm, Skolt Sami ǩiõtkâm.
Compare Lule Sami vuonev, Skolt Sami vueʹn.
The Atampaya dialect keeps mayi; Mpalitjanh, Yinwum and Linngithigh also have ayi.
